::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Decr 31st [1861]  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Katherine Wykes-Sneyd
:::

My dear [Irene](people/person_538.qmd)

I send back the translation with many thanks for the sight of it. I was very sorry to see by the paper that the sorrow you feared has come,[^1] and that the year is closing on you in sorrow and mourning, perhaps of a kind that one feels doubly, through one’s parents as well as oneself. I do not know whether you are feeling able to care for these Gosling matters now but I think I told [Pena](people/person_973.qmd) all about them.

The [Firefly](people/person_1168.qmd) and [Cobweb](people/person_675.qmd) had each three votes so they will each have an equal prize. Many thanks to you and [Glow Worm](people/person_534.qmd) for your photographs, hers is one of the best, and I am glad to have seen her brown eyes, and know the likeness

your affectionate

Mother Goose

---

[^1]: The death of her aunt [Grace (Fursdon) Rogers](people/person_1255.qmd) on 24 December 1861.
